requirements.requirement: opsadmin user configured on node1 with the specified ed25519 public key for SSH access
requirements.summary: opsadmin did not previously exist; it was created (cmd-04cc41d40ed04322) and the exact provided ed25519 key was installed into ~/.ssh/authorized_keys with correct ownership (opsadmin:opsadmin) and permissions (dir 700, file 600), confirmed by a root-privileged read (cmd-8bbe6b81260f4baa). Presence and content of the key were re-verified after the restart (cmd-1f0e278a02624e17).

requirements.requirement: SSH on node1 requires key-based authentication (no password fallback)
requirements.summary: Full sshd_config listing (cmd-e8f39669da564f32) shows PasswordAuthentication no and PubkeyAuthentication yes set globally with no Match blocks present anywhere in the file, and no sshd_config.d override directory exists (cmd-a16b4bf05a744342). Config was validated (sshd -t) and ssh restarted (cmd-dbe93f78ebac4f97). A live SSH attempt without the matching private key was rejected with 'Permission denied (publickey)' and no password prompt both before and after the restart (cmd-1ab5feeb903b4efb, cmd-d96ad3f31d004134). opsadmin's own password was additionally locked (cmd-e1029034fe1e44f7, confirmed cmd-8bbe6b81260f4baa) as defense-in-depth, eliminating any password fallback for that account specifically.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 (independent of the public task contract)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id f19de998-... with ssh active and opsadmin/key present (cmd-3603b1ac512844fc), matching the global before_prepare boot-identity snapshot. A backgrounded reboot returned an acknowledgement before disconnect (cmd-ca6f066c9f934d5e), the node became unreachable (cmd-39bf31e4807d4c3e), then came back with a new boot_id 4c125ee7-... (cmd-37143554c4be41f5), matching the global after_executor boot-identity snapshot. Post-restart checks confirmed ssh active, opsadmin and its key intact, password still locked, sshd config unchanged, and the negative SSH test still rejected with publickey-only denial (cmd-1f0e278a02624e17, cmd-d96ad3f31d004134). This constitutes a complete, cross-checked baseline/disruption/recovery cycle.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied both material outcomes of the task: opsadmin was created with the exact specified ed25519 key installed correctly, and SSH on node1 was confirmed (and remains) configured for key-only authentication with no password fallback, validated by both configuration inspection and live negative testing. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also completed with a full, cross-checked baseline → disruption → recovery cycle, showing the boot identity changed and all relevant state (user, key, password lock, sshd config, auth enforcement) survived the reboot intact.
limitations: The sshd_config's PasswordAuthentication no / PubkeyAuthentication yes settings appear to have pre-existed in the base image rather than being set by the executor; this is consistent with the task ('require key-based SSH authentication') being already satisfied by default, but the evidence does not include a prepare-phase snapshot distinguishing image defaults from prior state, since prepare was disabled and after_prepare is an alias of before_prepare.

No test was captured showing a successful SSH login using the actual matching private key for opsadmin (only negative tests without the key were shown), so full positive validation of key-based access relies on the correctness of the installed authorized_keys content rather than a demonstrated successful authenticated session.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map cleanly to task outcomes or the restart protocol: user creation, authorized_keys setup with correct ownership/permissions, password lock (a reasonable defense-in-depth step directly supporting 'require key-based SSH authentication' since it removes any password fallback for the specific account), and the reboot itself. sshd_config was found already compliant (PasswordAuthentication no / PubkeyAuthentication yes were pre-existing in the image, not modified by the executor), so no configuration mutation was needed there. The only minor note is that `systemctl restart ssh` (cmd-dbe93f78ebac4f97) was run even though no sshd_config change had been made — a low-risk, fully successful restart of an already-active service with no observed disruption or residue, so it does not rise to a meaningful hygiene concern. Lifecycle diffs show only expected boot-id-linked systemd-private tmp directories differing pre/post reboot, no failed services, no new listening sockets, and unchanged package-manager health — no executor-caused residue or damage.
